articleTitle: Simulation study for EIRP measurement of base-station antenna using simple phase retrieval technique
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this paper, the simulation study for an EIRP measurement technique of base-station antenna using the Fresnel region measurement method has been presented. We also apply a simple phase retrieval method for magnitude data obtained in one-plane. Base-station antennas installed in real environments unavoidably suffer farfield multipath interference, so the Fresnel region measurement method is optimal. From the simulation results, the transformed far-field pattern agreed closely with the reference far-field pattern.

articleTitle: Optimal dielectric antiradar coating for metallic plane and circular cylinder
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The problem of minimization of backscattering from bodies coated by a thin dielectric layer with complex permittivity is considered. For the cases of the plane and circular cylinder surfaces transcendental equations for optimal permittivity are numerically solved and analyzed. In particular, it is revealed that the asymptotical passage from the cylinder to the plane is seen in fact at not too large radii, only a little larger than ka = 2.

articleTitle: ACA method and SPAI preconditioner for acceleration BICGSTAB solver in MoM based solver TriD
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this paper effective acceleration technique for solving of electrically large EMC problems is described. It is known that for solving of large linear systems iterative solvers are very practical. The main problems for solution of such problems are related to large memory requirement for matrix and poor convergence of iterative solver. For solution of these problems the following techniques are applied: ACA (Adaptive Cross Approximation) technique for matrix compression and SPAI (Sparse Approximate Inverse) preconditioner to speed up convergence of iterative solver. For solving linear system BICGSTAB (Biconjugate Gradient Stabilised) solver is used. The advantages of considered solution are demonstrated using several numerical experiments.

articleTitle: Nonlinear spectral problems in synthesis theory of antennas with flat aperture
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Numerical method for solving the nonlinear two-parameter spectral problems arising in nonlinear synthesis theory of antennas with a flat radiating aperture is considered. The numerical algorithms to find the connected components of the spectrum of linear homogeneous two-dimensional integral equations, which describe the branching lines of solutions of the synthesis problems of flat apertures and antenna arrays according to the prescribed requirements to amplitude directivity pattern (DP) are constructed and justified. The analysis of branching of the solutions of basic equations of synthesis with use of proposed method is presented for the case of rectangular aperture. Results of numerical experiments are given.

articleTitle: Localization of the inhomogeneity in a two-way line
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The main objective of this paper is the analysis of the two-way line resonance properties, experiencing small variations of distributed parameters along its length. It is shown that the position of such variation can be determined from the AFC of the line. This paper continues the work described in [1]. The application field of described methodology is security intrusion detection systems.

articleTitle: Hilbert-Riemann problems in recovering parameters of a plane layered dielectric on conducting substrate
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: An inverse scattering problem for electromagnetic wave normal incidence on a plane layered structure with perfect conducting substrate is considered in the paper. The initial data is a frequency dependence of the reflection coefficient, phase characteristic of which provides information to extract optical depth of the structure and formulate two Hilbert-Riemann problems. Successive solutions of these problems allow reduction of the inverse problem to a trivial one, where both thickness and permittivity of layers are recovered from scattering coefficients in form of finite trigonometric series. Determination of electrical parameters and thickness of layered coatings that are used for electrical isolation and protection from corrosion of metal surfaces, is one of the most important problems of nondestructive evaluation. This problem is considered in the paper as an inverse scattering problem (ISP) for interaction of a plane electromagnetic wave with a plane layered dielectric on perfect conducting surface. Unlike the ISP for pure dielectrics, less attention is paid to the considered problem, although similar ISPs occur in many different applications [1, 2]. One of approaches is a treatment of the problem in time domain [3], where pulse response of the structure is considered only within period of wave propagation time until the pulse fully reflects from a perfect conducting substrate. Another idea of rigorous derivation of ISP solution is developed in the paper to represent the inverse problem as one for a pure dielectric medium with a piecewise-constant function of permittivity.

articleTitle: Web based research administration and information system
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The success of Research University highly depends on the well-conducted Research Administration and Management. Flexible and productive Research Management is one of basic points of modern university. Integrated scientific information system is a key future which could solve significant problem from the Research Administration and Management view-point in Georgia. Nowadays in Gerogia there is no comprehensive information about particular researcher as well as research Institute, or Institution of higher education. In turn it complicates both visiability and promotion of researcher's potential, establishement of communication with foreign colleagues and participation in joint research projects. In this article we consider research administration and information system developed at the Tbilisi State University from software engineering viewpoint. Different levels of the system and core modules are also discussed.

articleTitle: Using hybrid GPU algorithm for solving of EMC problems
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The state-of-art computer architecture is based on multi core processor technology. Nowadays processors contain even more than ten cores. On the other hand new technologies have emerged that enable using GPU in general propose computing. Moreover, GPUs have become easier to program, which allows developers to effectively exploit their computational power. Currently, major chip manufacturers are developing next generation microprocessor designs that integrate multi core CPU and GPU components. Thus, it has become essential to develop algorithms that effectively use both, CPU and GPU opportunities. This paper describes one of that such hybrid GPU algorithms that is used in EMC problem solution.

articleTitle: Scattering and generation of waves on non-linear cubically polarisable dielectric layer
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The problem of resonance scattering and generation of waves on an isotropic, non-magnetic, linearly E-polarised, non-linear, layered, cubically polarisable, dielectric structure, which is excited by a packet of plane waves, in the domain of resonance frequencies is considered. This problem is transformed to equivalent systems of non-linear problems, namely a system of one-dimensional non-linear Fredholm integral equations of the second kind and a system of non-linear boundary-value problems of Sturm-Liouville type. Results of the numerical investigation of the problem are presented.

articleTitle: Iterative solution of high-order boundary element method for acoustic problems
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A high-order boundary element method (BEM) for acoustic problems is presented in this paper. This method is based on the improved Burton-Miller formulation with high-order basis functions. The improved formulation successfully overcomes non-unique problems, and avoids the numerical difficulty of evaluating the hypersingular integral. It leads to the numerical implementations more efficient. Furthermore, the generalized minimal residual method (GMRES) and the efficient approximate inverse preconditioner are applied to accelerate the iterative solution of the BEM system. Several numerical examples clearly demonstrate the accuracy, efficiency and potentially application of the developed method for solving acoustic problems.

articleTitle: Application of multidimensional residues theory to determining number of solutions of transcendental equation systems arisen in phase optimization problems
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The subject of investigation is to determine the number of solutions to the system of transcendental equations related to a class of nonlinear integral equations of Hammerstein type with separated argument (phase) of unknown function. Such systems have arisen particularly in the phase optimization problems. The numerical algorithm is constructed and demonstrated on an example of equation of two complex unknowns.

articleTitle: Scattering of H-polarized electromagnetic wave by infinite dihedral wedge co-axially coupled with dielectric covered slotted cylinder
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Scattering of electromagnetic wave is considered for a composite structure consisting of an infinite dihedral wedge that is co-axially coupled with a dielectric covered slotted cylinder. The boundary-value method is employed using completeness property of the angular functions in the respective intervals. Problem is reduced to solution of system of algebraic equations of the second kind for the unknown coefficients of Fourier expansion of the scattered field. Analytical solution is obtained for certain value of cylinder slot-width. Scattered far-field and back radar cross section (BRCS) of the structure are evaluated asymptotically. The scattered field characteristics are also analyzed numerically with controlled precision. BRCS and the normalized radiation patterns of scattered field of narrow wedge for certain values of cylinder slot-width and electrical diameter of the cylinder are given.

articleTitle: Sound radiation from piston in fluid cylinder of finite length
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The exact solution of axial symmetric problem of harmonic sound wave radiation in a fluid cylinder of finite length with boundary impedance condition on lateral side is found. Generation of sound waves occurs due action from the baffled planar piston, which have an uniform vibration amplitude distribution and located on the acoustical rigid bottom of cylinder. The finite Fourier-Bessel integral transform is used over radial variable for the solving of problem. The complex amplitudes of acoustical pressure and components of particle displacement vector are obtained in the form of infinite Fourier-Bessel series. Numerical analysis of frequency and space distributions of spectral characteristics of acoustic field are carried out.

articleTitle: Solution of searched function and its normal derivative jump problem for the Laplacian in R3 by means of simple and double layer potentials
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Modeling of electrostatic fields at the environments with different characters leads to necessity of solution of the jump problems with inclined derivative for the Laplacian in R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. This problem at the Hilbert space the normal derivative elements of which has the jump through boundary surface was considered in [2]. Solution of this problem was searched as simple layer potential. At the Hilbert space the elements of which have the jump through boundary surface such problem was considered in [4]. Solution of this problem was searched as double layer potential. The searched function and its derivative jump problem at the Hilbert space elements of which as their normal derivatives has the jump through boundary surface are considered at this article. The conditions of well-posed solution of formulated problem are determined. We suggest to look for the solution of this problem as the sum of simple and double layer potentials. We define the conditions of the well-posed solution of the later.

articleTitle: Variants of transparent antennas
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Calculations and simulation results for different transparent antennas are presented. The concrete variant of the antenna is offered.

articleTitle: Analysis of a compact printed TPMS antenna in complex environment
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid MoM with a multilayered Green's function is applied to electromagnetic (EM) modeling of a printed tire pressure monitoring system (TMPS) antenna. The simulated results for this antenna are shown to be in a good agreement with measurements. Modeling of TMPS antenna in complex environment of automobile is conducted, and predictions of EM behavior of TMPS antenna mounted on the tires and integrated in a full automobile geometry are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Antenna synthesis with limitations in the Fresnel region
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Properties of the electromagnetic field of radiation systems change with distance from source: the near region, the Fresnel region and the far region are considered in the antenna theory. The formulations of most antenna synthesis problems include some requirements on characteristics of electromagnetic field in the far region, for example, on the amplitude directivity pattern [1]. Today in the connection with electromagnetic ecology problems, synthesis tasks which include the decreasing of the antenna radiation in the Fresnel region become more actually. In this paper is investigated the synthesis problem of the cylindrical radiator by the given amplitude directivity pattern in the far region with some limitations on radiation in the Fresnel region.

articleTitle: Nonlinear interaction of two Fano-shape resonances in bilayered planar metamaterial with fish scale structure
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The nonlinear interaction of two Fano-shape resonances in the bilayered structure made of two gratings of planar perfectly conducting infinite strips placed on both sides of the Kerr-type nonlinear dielectric slab is analyzed. The first resonance is obtained due to the trapped-mode excitation in each grating of curvilinear strips. The second one is a result of the interaction of the antiphased current oscillations between two adjacent gratings. It is demonstrated that these two resonances react differently on the applied intense light which can lead to their overlapping.

articleTitle: Enhancement of absorption bistability by planar metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: We report on the peculiarities of the absorption bistability which appears in a planar metamaterial composed of a 4-fold periodic array of two concentric metal rings placed on a substrate of saturate absorbing material. Such structure bears the Fano-shape resonance of a trapped-mode excitation which is a result of the antiphase current oscillations in the elements of a periodic cell. It is demonstrated that the switching can be achieved between essentially different levels of transmission nearly the frequency of this resonance excitation.

articleTitle: Fractal transformation of the Hertz dipole in the EH-vibrator
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In paper transition from a fractal Hertz-dipole to the EH-vibrator for the first time is theoretically shown. Examination is carried out with the help differintegral model operations fractal α-pole. Examples of numerical calculations of scaling indexes for a classical dipole and fractal α-pole are given.

articleTitle: Inverse problem for structures having both continuous permittivity variation intervals and steps
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The effective method for reconstruction of permittivity profile of structures having both intervals of continuous ε(x) distribution and sharp interfaces is proposed. The method is nonstandard modification of Newton-Kantorovich iterative scheme applied to Riccati differential equation supposing piecewise-square-hyperbolic permittivity profile. The modification is compared with previously developed one supposing piecewise-constant permittivity profile on numerically synthesized reflection-coefficient data for complicated structure.

articleTitle: Combining of fourier-laguerre method with boundary elements method for the numerical solution of mixed problems for wave equation
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Combining of Fourier-Laguerre method with boundary elements method for the numerical solution of mixed problems for wave equation is presented.

articleTitle: Losses of energy of two counter - propagating transverse - magnetic waves in the absorbing plate in a waveguide
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The propagation of two transverse - magnetic (TM) waves with different initial phases in the regular ideal waveguide, where is placed the absorbing plate, is considered. Supposed, that two coherent waves have opposite directions of propagation. The losses of energy in the absorbing plate are found. Some aspects of tunnel interference in the absorbing plate in the waveguide are discovered.

articleTitle: Comparison of subdomain functions in the moment method for quasiperiodic waveguiding structures
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Phenomena of coupling of wave paraxial beam and quasisurface wave at perfectly conducting plane with segment of spatially oscillating surface impedance is considered. Integral equation for perturbed current distribution is obtained. Method of moments is used. Solution was expanded in terms of subdomain basis functions. Various types of subdomain functions are compared in form of a combination of atomic function and the Lagrangian interpolating polynomials. Advantages of subdomain functions of higher order were demonstrated.

articleTitle: MAS simulation of plasmon coupling in nanosphere pairs
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Plasmonic structures are very attractive in many applications. From other side numerical simulations of plasmonic structures are very demanding and expensive in terms of memory and CPU time, making the selection of a suitable numerical method for the field computation important. The numerical problems are caused because optical nanostructures based on metal parts exhibit strong material dispersion, loss, and plasmon-polariton effects that require a very accurate numerical simulation. To examine this problem, we applied Method of Auxiliary Sources (MAS) to a group of 3D plasmonic nanoshpere problems.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional Gaussian beam with circular cross-section scattered from a gyrotropic slab
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The problem of the scattering of 3-D Gaussian beam incident at an arbitrary angle onto a gyrotropic slab has been formulated and solved. The new formulas for the scattered 3-D Gaussian beam fields in the form of the single integrals have been derived. They allow to reduce the time spent upon the numerical calculations of the scattered beam fields.

articleTitle: Scattering of TE10 mode in an E-plane waveguide bend with jump of permittivity
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A fullwave generalized scattering matrix (GSM) analysis of an asymmetrical E-plane junction of hollow and filled rectangular waveguides is presented. Properties of the structure are compared with the properties of the waveguide traversed by a slanted interface between two media. The ability to study the configurations of this type with the help of a scalar approximation is also examined.

articleTitle: Autocollimation regime on a reflect array of short-circuited coaxial-sector waveguides
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Autocollimation regime in the reflection of electromagnetic waves from the array of short-circuited coaxial-sector waveguides is investigated. The possibility of transforming power of the incident wave in power of the autocollimator wave is shown possible. Polarization characteristics of the autocollimator wave are calculated.

articleTitle: Eigen-modes of the linearized problems of scattering and generation of waves on non-linear layer
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The problem of scattering and generation of waves on an isotropic, non-magnetic, linearly E-polarised, non-linear, layered, cubically polarisable, dielectric structure, which is excited by a plane wave, is investigated in the domain of resonance frequencies. The analytical continuation of these linear problems into the region of complex values of the frequency parameter allows us to switch to the analysis of spectral problems. Results of the numerical investigation of the problem are presented.

articleTitle: System of integro-transcendetnal equations in case of vanishing solution of free phase problem
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A nonlinear integral equation of Hammerstein type arising in the so called modified phase problem is considered. Solutions of the equation are represented by means of polynomials of finite degree describing zeros of these solutions. For the case of solutions vanishing in the considered interval, new system of transcendental and integral equations is obtained.

articleTitle: Effective boundary conditions for a straight thin-walled elastic inclusion of low contrast in the thin plate
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Effective boundary conditions for flexural waves scattering by a straight thin-walled inclusion of low contrast in a thin plate are considered. Explicit forms of the first-order approximate boundary conditions are derived using Kirchhoff plate theory. The methodology of investigation is based on the method of matched asymptotic expansions with the thickness-to-length ratio as the perturbation parameter.

articleTitle: Models of reliability parameters of compound electromagnetic systems
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Main probabilistic parameters for reliability evaluation of compound electromagnetic systems are examined in this paper. Models in the form of recurrent expressions are worked out for the probability distribution calculation of count of operating output elements and for the failure frequency in the case when the lifetime of ageing output elements is circumscribed by the Weibull distribution.

articleTitle: Transparent antennas
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The equation for the current along the transparent metal radiator is written and solved. On the base of the equation solution the currents distribution along the radiator axis was analyzed.

articleTitle: Application of hybrid MOM and multilayered Green's function to EM modeling of printed microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid MOM with a multilayered Green's function is applied to electromagnetic (EM) modeling of printed microstrip antennas (PMA). This approach is validated on ultra-wideband (UWB) PMA, and a good agreement between the simulated and measured results is shown. Some predictions of EM behavior of UWB PMA integrated in a real car model are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Inversion of a prolate metallic object's orientation with the Gauss-Newton minimization algorithm
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This paper presents numerical results of the Gauss-Newton minimization algorithm application to inversion of an orientation of the metallic object with an oblong form. The Method of Auxiliary Sources (MAS) is used to obtain the synthetic data of the electromagnetic induction (EMI) in conducted numerical investigations. In the studies, presented here, it is assumed that electromagnetic and geometrical parameters of the object, such as conductivity, magnetic permeability, dimensions and the distance between the sensor and object's center are known. The approach is applied on inversion of object's orientation using noisy and noisy free synthetic data.

articleTitle: Near field of plane aperture
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The problem on calculation of the field in the whole half-space (including the near zone) by its tangent electric components given on the aperture plane is considered. The standard technique based on the (scalar and vector) Green functions is applied. The results are valid at any finite distance from the aperture plane. Passing to the limit z → 0 is checked.

articleTitle: On ray optics equations for analysis of the waves refraction in fractal medium
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Ray optics method for the solution of problems for terahertz waves is dilated in the report. The electromagnetic field differintegral model is applied to entry of Maxwell equations and an eikonal, which are applicable for solution of electromagnetic wave refraction problem in fractal medium.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of the computed SAR and temperature rise to the em exposure child and adult man
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to analyze realistic exposure scenarios for a child model by means of numerical computations. Our aim is to determine and compare peak values of SAR and temperature rise for child human model and compare them to results for the adult human model [1].

articleTitle: Stability and convergence analysis of model state variable trajectories of analogue KWTA neural circuit
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A continuous-time mathematical model of K -winners-take-all (KWTA) neural circuit consisting of the state equation with discontinuous right-hand side and output equations is described. Stability and convergence analysis of the model state variable trajectories is performed by means of the Persidskij form of the state equation in conjunction with the associated Lyapunov function. According to analytical derivation the model is globally stable with a finite convergence time. The model can process any finite distinct signals with arbitrary specified minimal speed that is controlled by its single parameter. The model states do not depend on initial conditions and possess signal order preserving property. Simulation results confirm theoretical derivations and demonstrate good performance of the model.

articleTitle: The electromagnetic properties of the infinite periodic lattice embedded in the dielectric layer
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In 2010 at the DIPED International Seminar/Workshop there was presented the theoretical part for the diffraction problem of the plane wave on the 2D periodical infinite lattice located in the free space [1]. The lattice element represented the conducting wire with the resonant properties. In the first part of this paper we consider the theoretical background for the same lattice embedded in the dielectric with finite width layer. As the dielectric also has resonant properties this will amplify the resonant effects of the whole structure. The final idea of this study is the next: based on computer simulation to find out the best parameters of the structure to get necessary properties of the complex materials. We have created program package for the simplified case when the lattice is located in the free area and in the second part of this paper some numerical results are presented.

articleTitle: Interaction of electromagnetic wave with a composite semiconductor structure
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The interaction of electromagnetic wave with a composite semiconductor structure formed by dielectric layers, diffraction grating film GaAs (CS) is investigated. The reflection and transmission coefficients have been obtained for the structure.

articleTitle: Application of generalized method of eigenoscillations to problems of nanoplasmonics
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A version of generalized eigenoscillation method is applied to the problem about resonant effects in metallic nanoparticles. An approach is proposed, that permits to avoid calculating all higher eigenoscillations except the resonant one. An algorithm for determination of the resonant eigenoscillation, based on the Galerkin procedure, is described in details for the case of bodies of revolution. Model numerical results are presented.

articleTitle: The algorithm for the characteristics calculating of the three-dimensional gaussian wave beams scattering on the flat screens of finite thickness of rectangular holes
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The diffraction problem of three-dimensional Gaussian beam on the flat screens of finite thickness of rectangular holes is solved. A new algorithm for calculating scattered fields of beam is proposed. The conditions under which the distortion of the reflected field pattern and the narrowing of the transmitted field pattern appear are studied.

articleTitle: Quasi-periodic Bragg structures with thin lossy layers
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The behavior of quasi-periodic and aperiodic (chirp) Bragg structures with thin lossy layers has been considered. In order to calculate the dependence of the reflection coefficient against frequency, transmission matrix method was used. A deep minimum of reflection coefficient for any frequency is implemented by proper choice of the thickness of the last thin film and its optical distance to the substrate. The possibility of providing broadband reflection by aperiodic structures has been offered.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic research environment (EMagRE) - Crossplatform EM software package based on FDTD method
publicationTitle: 2011 XVIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: We present cross platform programm package with memory efficient implementation of Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method. Component modules implementation of the package is also presented.
